note: Per-CROP-TYPE seasonal LIFT deadlines for 'single'-habit storage crops — the crops isReadyToPick() structurally cannot surface (harvestReadiness.js requires harvest_habit IN ('repeat','cut_and_come_again') AND >=1 prior harvest, so every once-per-season crop is invisible to the ready band). Keyed by crop_types.slug, same key space as harvest-attributes-v1.json. THIS FILE IS DELIBERATELY ALMOST EMPTY. A date with no citable source is not a date; the disconfirmations in `no_calendar_deadline` are as load-bearing as the one record in `by_crop_type` and exist so the next session does not re-derive the falsified premise from scratch.
provenance_rule: Every entry in by_crop_type carries source + source_url + confidence, and its `true_trigger` names the physical signal the calendar date is only a PROXY for. Where the trigger is an observed plant state the app does not record, the crop belongs in no_calendar_deadline, NOT in by_crop_type with an invented date. Precedent for the harm: harvestWindows.json shipped at 11.8% cultivar calibration with 22-day median error.
frost_anchor_warning: These deadlines are RELATED to FROST_ANCHORS.firstFallFrost (src/lib/sowEngine.js, '09-28') but are not derived from it, and the relation is per-crop. For sweet potato the binding constraint is VINE KILL, not soil temperature: once frost blackens the vines the roots begin degrading in the ground regardless of how warm the soil still is, so the lift must land BEFORE the frost anchor, not after it. That is a reversal of this file's original 1.0.0 reasoning, which anchored on soil temperature and put the deadline 17 days LATER than first frost — 17 days after the crop was already lost (Dave, 2026-08-17, BUG-SWEETPOTATODEADLINE-001). storageDeadlines.test.js pins the new ordering; do NOT reintroduce a deadline later than the frost anchor for a frost-sensitive crop, and do NOT blanket-derive every crop from the anchor either — the frost-tolerant roots in no_calendar_deadline correctly have no frost deadline at all.

field_contract.deadline_kind: regional_calendar_proxy = a calendar date a regional extension source states as the practical cutoff, standing in for a physical trigger the app cannot measure. No other kind is defined yet; do not invent one.
field_contract.deadline_month_day: MM-DD. Resolved against the year of the caller-supplied today, never against an internal clock.
field_contract.check_from_month_day: MM-DD the CHECK window opens. Always earlier than deadline_month_day. The gap is deliberate lead time, not a second deadline.
field_contract.true_trigger: The physical signal the date proxies for. Prose, for display and for honesty — the date is downstream of this, not the other way round.
field_contract.loss: What is actually lost, and when it becomes visible. Storage-crop loss materialises months later in the pantry, which is why it needs surfacing at all.
field_contract.check_copy / past_copy: User-facing copy. CHECK FORM ONLY — 'start checking X', never 'X is ready'. These estimates are weak and the copy must not overclaim.
field_contract.confidence: high | medium | low. medium = a regional extension source states the guidance, but as a typical case ('usually before...'), not a measured threshold.

sweet_potato.true_trigger: Vine kill, not soil temperature. Frost blackens the vines well before the soil cools, and once the vines are dead the roots begin degrading in the ground — decay enters through the crown and the roots will not store, however warm the soil still is. The published soil thresholds (growth stops below 65F, chilling injury below 55F) are real but they are not what closes the window first in 5b.
sweet_potato.loss: The whole stored crop, invisible at harvest. Roots left in after vine kill rot from the crown; chilled roots show shrivelled, sunken, dark areas and blacken when cut, and 'hardcore' roots stay hard after cooking. The damage is permanent and only shows up in storage.
sweet_potato.check_copy: Start checking sweet potatoes for lifting — frost kills the vines and the roots start going the moment it does, so they want to be out of the ground before the first frost, usually by late September.
sweet_potato.past_copy: Sweet potato lifting window has passed — worth checking whether any are still in the ground.
sweet_potato.source: UMass Extension — Sweet Potato Harvest and Storage, plus Dave's zone-5b vine-kill call (2026-08-17, BUG-SWEETPOTATODEADLINE-001)
sweet_potato.notes: SUPERSEDES the 1.0.0 date of 10-15. That date encoded UMass's 'usually before mid-October' phrase, which reads as a soil-temperature cutoff and lands 17 days AFTER FROST_ANCHORS.firstFallFrost ('09-28') — i.e. two and a half weeks after frost has already killed the vines and started the roots degrading. Dave's ruling 2026-08-17: in zone 5b the binding constraint is vine kill, so lift within 24-48h of the vines blackening and set the calendar proxy just ahead of the frost anchor. 09-25 is firstFallFrost - 3d, giving a margin for a frost that arrives early; the check window keeps the same 14-day lead the 1.0.0 record used. Still `medium` — it is a regional typical case standing in for an observed vine state the app does not record, not a measured threshold. Dave has 2 live sweet potato plantings (verified live prod 2026-08-12), both status 'vegetative'.

no_calendar_deadline._note: Crops examined for V4-STORAGEDEADLINE-001 and deliberately NOT given a date. Each records WHY and what signal would have to exist first. Removing a crop from this list requires a citable regional source, not a plausible guess.

winter_squash.design_claim: 'off the vine before frost touches fruit or it will not store'
winter_squash.finding: Not supported by the regional source. The UMass pumpkin/winter-squash fact sheet gives no frost or freeze guidance at all; its cold threshold is 50F CHILLING INJURY IN STORAGE, a post-harvest condition. Penn State puts field damage at a HARD FREEZE below 28F, which is a materially colder and later event than 'frost'. Also moot for now: 0 live winter_squash plantings in prod (verified 2026-08-12).
winter_squash.needed: A regional source giving a field-frost threshold for storage life, plus at least one live planting to surface it on.

bean_dry.design_claim: 'in at pod-rattle before the next wetting'
bean_dry.finding: Dave does not grow dry beans. All 3 live `bean` plantings are snap/filet bush types (Contender, Gold Rush, Tavera), and crop_types.bean is harvest_habit='repeat' — so they are already visible to the ready-to-pick band and are not a storage crop at all. There is no dry-bean crop type.
bean_dry.needed: A dry-bean crop type and a live planting. The trigger (pod rattle) is an observed state the schema does not record.

garlic.design_claim: 'cure then move before humidity re-softens wrappers'
garlic.finding: Garlic is the ONE crop already carrying a hard window: crop_types.harvest_season_start_doy=186 / end_doy=211 = 2026-07-05 to 2026-07-30. That window closed before this item was filed. Zero garlic harvests have ever been logged, and the single live planting is still status 'vegetative'. A deadline feature cannot help 2026 garlic; it would fire on a window already 13 days shut.
garlic.needed: Nothing new for the harvest deadline — it exists. The CURING stage the claim is actually about is a post-harvest process with no schema representation at all.

onion.design_claim: 'lift within 10-14d of leaf-fall or necks rot and the crop will not store'
onion.finding: The trigger is leaf-fall (tops going over) — an OBSERVED PLANT STATE. There is no leaf_fall event type in event_log (38 types in prod, none of them this), so the 10-14 day clock has nothing to start from. A calendar substitute would be a guess. Separately, the premise that these close invisibly did not hold: Dave lifted onions on 07-27, 07-28 and 08-04 with no app prompt.
onion.needed: A leaf-fall / tops-down observation event type. Then the deadline is derived, not invented.

shallot.finding: Same unrecorded leaf-fall trigger. Same disconfirmation, more strongly: Dave lifted shallots on 07-23, 07-26, 07-30, 08-04 and 08-08 — five separate picks, incrementally, unprompted. The observed behaviour is continuous pulling as needed, not a single storage lift on a deadline.

cabbage.finding: The trigger is a rainfall EVENT crossed with head maturity. event_log has a `rain` type (723 rows) but no rainfall depth that would distinguish 'heavy' from any rain, and no head-maturity signal. This is a weather-reactive alert, not a seasonal deadline — it does not belong in a deadline dataset even once buildable. Cabbage is also frost-tolerant, so no fall date applies.
cabbage.needed: Rainfall depth on rain events plus a head-formed signal. Belongs to a weather-alert feature, not this one.

potato.finding: Examined and rejected. UMass gives harvest conditions (soil 45-65F, tuber 50-60F) and a 10-14 day skin-set hold after vine kill, but NO calendar cutoff. Tubers are unharmed by the frost that kills the vines; the real limit is ground freeze, far later than first frost and not anchored anywhere in the app. 3 live plantings.
potato.needed: A ground-freeze anchor, which the app does not have. FROST_ANCHORS has no such field.

carrot.finding: Frost-tolerant and deliberately left in ground — extension guidance is to hold carrots in the soil UNTIL frost and harvest before the ground freezes. A first-frost deadline would be actively wrong: it would pull a crop that improves. 3 live plantings.
carrot.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.

beet.finding: Recovers from 1-2 light freezings; guidance is to harvest before the first MODERATE freeze or mulch for winter harvest. No first-frost deadline. Dave picked beets on 07-16, 07-31 (x2) and 08-04 unprompted. 2 live plantings.
beet.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.

leek.finding: The most frost-tolerant of the set — some varieties take temperatures near 20F, and delaying harvest past first frost is the recommended practice. crop_types.loss_horizon_hours=1440 (60 days) already encodes that it holds. 2 live plantings.
leek.needed: Nothing. This crop correctly has no deadline.
